cards.headline:
SonicFox pulls out of Nexcon
over its AI promo art
cards.body: Fighting game savant SonicFox terminated their Nexcon contract after the event used AI art in its promotion.

blocks.x: Upon discovering that Nexcon, a gaming event taking place in Oklahoma next month at which fighting game savant Dominique “SonicFox” McLean was set to be a special guest, had used AI art for promotional purposes, McLean promptly pulled out.

“Not sure who’s in charge of Nexcon, but I absolutely refuse to have my likeness be AI generated and my interest in attending as a special guest has dropped to 0,” McLean wrote on Twitter. “Incredibly disrespectful.” The same day, they added that they’d terminated their contract and would no longer be attending.

Ty Bailey of Ninjutsu Entertainment, the organization putting on Nexcon, posted a video apologizing to McLean, explaining that Ninjutsu only resorted to AI because it had run out of money to pay human artists, and implored SonicFox to reconsider.

McLean held firm. “I’m a forgiving person, and I can hear the remorse in your voice so I forgive you. However, there are still consequences to said actions that will prompt me not to attend. Use the money you offered me in contract to hire artists, and maybe next year I’ll reconsider.”
“If all goes well and you build a community with willing artists and talent and remove all AI, I may be more amenable to next year,” they continued.
